meaning: (1) the son of Bartholomew, from the nick. Bartle and pet Bartl-ey; (2) of Berkeley, a variant
author_comment: cf. Charlie, Teddy, Bobbie, &c. Although looking strongly local, I find no evidence of this. We have, on the contrary, proof that Bartley owns Bartholomew as its parent. [Bartly Bradforth, co. York. W. 9.] This occurring in the county where Bartle was so popular clinches the argument; v. Bartle, Bartlett, Bate, &c. In the above two entries [under (2)] we see evidence that the west-country surname Berkeley was sometimes modified into Bartley.
source: Fabric Rolls of York Minster: Wills and Inventories (Surtees Society)
